newsitem.title: VATICAN: Castro arrives at Vatican for papal audience.
newsitem.headline: Castro arrives at Vatican for papal audience.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro arrived at the Vatican on Tuesday for an historic meeting with Pope John Paul, witnesses said.
The communist leader's heavily-armed motorcade entered the Vatican at 10:45 a.m. (0945 GMT) to take Castro to the papal apartments.

The meeting between the two men was due to begin at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT). It is expected to lead almost certainly to the first trip by a pope to Cuba, where church-state relations have been sometimes frosty since Castro took over in 1959.

Vatican sources said they expected the Pope to press Castro to implement democratic reforms and to allow more freedom of movement for the Catholic Church. The Vatican cancelled all media access for the audience about an hour before it began.

The encounter between the veteran revolutionary, 70, and the anti-communist Polish Pope, 76, is potentially the most significant audience since the Catholic leader received then Soviet President Mikhail Grobachev in 1989.
That meeting took place as the Iron Curtain began to crumble and it later led to new freedoms for religious believers throughout the then Soviet union.
